one_pager.big_idea: Before we believe a claim, we ask what kind of claim it is and whether evidence could ever check it.
goals: I can sort claims into fact, opinion, testable and not testable, and explain my choice.
I can use Claim, Evidence, Reasoning and the three-point verdict scale to judge a claim.

flow.what: Seat groups of 4 at fixed tables for the series and give out role cards; explain 'no exams, lots of thinking'. Slides 1 to 2.
Give out the Year 9 skills check, read the instructions aloud and keep time; students work alone and in silence. Reassure: 'This is to show your growth, not a test score.' Slide 3.
Give out the survey and read each statement aloud in English; students mark one face per statement. Slide 4.
'Can you see the Great Wall from the Moon with your eyes alone?' Hands-up vote: Yes, No or Not sure; tell a partner why (any language). Do not reveal. Slide 5.

Four kinds of claim with the flowchart, then Claim, Evidence, Reasoning and the verdict scale; students repeat key words and answer quick 'fact or opinion?' questions with fingers (1 to 4). Slides 6 to 8.

Claim sort in groups: 16 cards on the A3 sorting mat (4 boxes plus the 'We argued' strip); record the sort on the worksheet (Core), then Stretch or Challenge. Teacher challenges with 'Could any evidence show that is wrong?' Slide 9.
Back to the Great Wall: show the evidence, model a CER and ask for a verdict (expected: Not supported); partners share one sentence with a frame; exit ticket collected. Slides 10 to 11.

one_pager.practical: Claim sort: each group reads 16 claim cards (A to P) aloud, uses the flowchart to place them on an A3 mat as Opinion, Fact, Testable or Not testable, puts disputed cards in the 'We argued' strip and records the sort on the worksheet. One short activity only this week.
one_pager.assessment: Baseline skills check (15 minutes, marked out of 20, into the progress tracker; papers filed and not returned before Week 10); interest survey (into the tracker survey tab); exit ticket: can each student tell testable from not testable (quick check for Week 2 grouping). No logbook line this week: the logbook starts in Week 2.
hazards: No practical hazards beyond normal classroom rules.
one_pager.language_note: Frames: 'This claim is testable because we could measure ___.' 'This is an opinion because ___.' 'Our verdict is ___ because ___.' Chinese talk is welcome during the sort and the Hook pair talk; groups report back in English with a frame. Skills check: read questions aloud and explain everyday words, but do not explain science words; Chinese is accepted for explanations (Questions 4, 8, 9 and 10). Traps: 'fact' here means 'checked many times', not 'anything I am sure about'; 'verdict' is the final decision on a claim; 'testable' does not mean 'true'.
watch_out: The skills check and survey are fixed. If time is short, cut the Challenge section, run the Great Wall verdict as a 1-minute teacher model, and let groups sort only cards A to L.
'If it is not testable, it must be false.' No: not testable means evidence cannot decide, so scientists cannot say either way. 'Not enough evidence yet' is an honest answer, not a failure.
Card J is the planted trap: a claim about opinions is testable with a survey. Card L (Great Wall) placed under Fact shows a popular myth: make sure at least one group explains each card to the class.
Do not go through, hand back or display the skills check answers: the same paper is used again in Week 10.
one_pager.next_week_link: Week 2 builds on 'evidence beats belief' by showing how our own brains can be fooled; the verdict scale is used again and students start the logbook. Mark the skills checks, enter tracker columns I to O and file the papers.

Worksheet (design Main and Worksheet-2): Core 2 on page 1 says 'Use the word bank at the bottom of the page', but the fold-under word bank is at the foot of page 2. The exit ticket strip at the foot of page 2 backs onto Stretch 2 at the foot of page 1, so cutting or tearing it off removes part of page 1. Collect the whole worksheet instead, or move the strip?

Role cards: Y9_W01 and the kit card list '1 set of 5' per group with no print spec; the design (Role-cards) is one A4 sheet of 5 cards, 85 x 55 mm. Paper or card, and laminated or not? The Teacher Guide language pass adds 'role cards with duties and buddy cards', but its prep calendar says 'No change' for Year 9: confirm Year 9 uses the 5-card set.

Role card wording: the designed Safety Officer card says 'Check goggles are on' and 'Lead the clean-up', but the Teacher Guide gives the job as 'Checks the kit card and safety rules', and Y9_W01 has Recorders (not Safety Officers) check the cards back in.
Survey wording: Y9_W01 (lesson plan and Slide 4) says 'circle one face'; Interest_Survey.md and the designed sheet say 'Tick ONE face'.

The Teacher Guide prep calendar ('Before Week 1', all years) also lists printing logbooks and name cards. Y9_W01 uses neither (the Year 9 logbook starts in Week 2; name cards are not mentioned in the Year 9 file), so they are not entered here. Are name cards wanted for Year 9?
No spares are stated for worksheets, skills checks or surveys (24 of each entered). Add spares for new students?
Where are the claim card envelopes, mats and role card sets kept between lessons? The Teacher Guide's class box is described for logbooks only, and the kit card does not say.
